# `lost-error-context`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: strict · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a catch that maps every failure to one replacement error without using
the captured original error.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Collapsing distinct failures removes evidence needed for diagnosis and can make
callers handle the wrong abstraction.

## When it fires

Enable it at error-boundary code where preserving identity, logging context, or
deliberate translation is expected. An operation that can fail in only one way
loses nothing when that error keeps its name (`allocator.alloc(...) catch
return error.OutOfMemory`) or when checked arithmetic's `error.Overflow`
becomes a domain limit (`std.math.add(...) catch return error.TooLarge`), so
these are not reported. The single error is known for `std.math` arithmetic,
allocator methods, and functions the file declares once with a one-error set
(`Allocator.Error`, `error{Name}` or an alias of either).

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn load() !void {
    return error.Failed;
}

fn open() !void {
    load() catch return error.LoadFailed;
}
```

Reference: <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/#Errors>
